transcript.text: Right, Mia, Sam, let's go through your project on recycling around the campus. Where did you begin?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: It was harder than I thought, honestly. We had a lot of ideas at the beginning, but we had to decide which ones were realistic.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: That's a common experience. Planning is often the most difficult stage of any project.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: Well, first we wanted to know how much waste the university actually produces, but the office couldn't give us the figures.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: Yes, that was frustrating. So in the end we counted the bags of rubbish in three buildings for one week.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Good thinking. And what did you find?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: We also took photographs of the bins in each building, so we could show the differences in the final video.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Photographs are a good idea. Visual evidence is much more convincing than a table of numbers.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: Mostly paper and plastic bottles. About sixty percent of everything we counted could have been recycled.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: The surprising thing was that most students said they recycle at home but not at university.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Why do you think that is?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: We asked about forty students in the canteen, and a few of them seemed quite embarrassed about their answers.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: That's interesting. People often feel guilty when they are asked about their habits.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: I'd say it's mainly because the bins are hard to find. People don't want to carry a bottle around for ten minutes.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: Right. And the bins that exist are all the same grey colour, so nobody knows what goes where.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: The cleaners told us the same thing, actually. They spend a lot of time sorting bags that students have filled in a hurry.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: So the cleaners could be a useful source for your report, too.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: So what are you recommending?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: For the library, we'd suggest putting up posters, because students sit there for hours and have time to read them.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: In the canteen the main issue is plastic cups, so we want to ask for reusable cups with a small discount.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Mm, a discount might work. Did you think about the dormitories?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: Yes. There the problem is that everything goes in one bin, so we'd like colour-coded labels on every bin. We did hear complaints about paperwork too, but that seemed less important.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: For the lecture halls, we thought about fines, but Mia convinced me that's too negative, so we suggest reward points instead.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Reward points. Interesting. And the sports centre?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: There are lots of water bottles there, so we'd like volunteers from the sports clubs to collect them after matches.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: Do you think the sports clubs will agree? They are usually very busy during the season.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: We spoke to two captains already, and they were quite positive, as long as it doesn't take too much of their time.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: That sounds sensible. How will you present the results?
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: We were going to make a long report, but Dr Hall, you told us last week that a short video is better.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: I did. Most people will not read thirty pages, but they will watch three minutes.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: So we'll make a video and put a one-page summary on the student website.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: Excellent. Send me your draft by Friday and we'll meet again on Monday.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr Hall. We're both really looking forward to seeing the finished video.
transcript.speaker: MIA

transcript.text: So am I. It's a project that could genuinely change how the campus works.
transcript.speaker: DR HALL
